question: Which remaining Android-node high-authority capabilities should OpenClaw accept, and under what trust boundary: device.control, ADB-style access, arbitrary/dynamic program execution, or only a narrower node-hosted tool contract?
rationale: The remaining work changes Android device authority and remote execution rather than fixing broken existing behavior, so automation cannot choose the permanent product/security boundary.

options.title: Split and design the Android authority boundary
options.body: Keep this issue open and require separate security-reviewed designs or PRs for device control, ADB, and dynamic execution before implementation.

options.title: Route dynamic tools through the generic node-hosted tools path
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90431 or its successor for generic dynamic tool exposure, while keeping Android device-control and ADB decisions separate.

options.title: Decline Android execution/control in core for now
options.body: Explicitly reject ADB/dynamic execution and close or narrow this roadmap to low-risk Android diagnostics only.

recommendation.title: Split and design the Android authority boundary
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require separate security-reviewed designs or PRs for device control, ADB, and dynamic execution before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses the node/Gateway/tool trust boundary where steipete has the clearest adjacent ownership signal through the open node-hosted tools candidate and recent Android history.
